pr_title: Added python packages in user directories
pr_body:
Added `uid` column to `python_packages`. This makes it easy to scan for packages in user directories. 

Fixes https://github.com/osquery/osquery/issues/8500
From Fleet: https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/issues/24805

I included some user directories that were missing in the initial scan. `.pyenv` places its python packages in the user directory as well as doing a pip install with the `--user` [flag](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/#cmdoption-user) with the homebrew installed python. Here are two example paths from my mac:
`/Users/ksykulev/.pyenv/versions/3.13.1/lib/python3.13/site-packages`
`/Users/ksykulev/Library/Python/3.13/lib/python/site-packages`
pr_comments:
The committers listed above are authorized under a signed CLA.
  • :white_check_mark: login: ksykulev / name: Konstantin Sykulev (ec1103b033e019cdfb30004f8b43ef638a5330e6)
`select uid, name, path from users cross join python_packages using(uid);` Appears to be pulling all user directories mentioned in #8500:

A note about performance. When using the users cross join approach it must iterate through the entire user table which can cause some performance degradation. Here are some numbers on my macbook m3 with 129 users. This could probably use some optimization in the future, but can be avoided with the proper query.

| root  | python_packages  | Run Time: real 0.052 user 0.011503 sys 0.040453 |

| root | cross join python_packages |  Run Time: real 4.332 user 0.986408 sys 3.187372 |
| root |  excluding users, cross join python_packages | Run Time: real 0.284 user 0.056777 sys 0.158205 |

As root, excluding some users that will never have python packages. For reference this query came from the fleet repository:
https://github.com/fleetdm/fleet/blob/main/server/service/osquery_utils/queries.go#L804-L807
```
osquery> WITH cached_users AS (
```

issue_context.title: python_packages table returning incomplete results
issue_context.body: # Bug report ### What operating system and version are you using? Darwin 15.1.1, macOS Sonoma 14.6.1 ### What version of osquery are you using? 5.14.1 ### What steps did you take to reproduce the issue? SELECT * from python_packages returns only a few results: ### What did you expect to see? `pip3 list` shows 120 installed. ### What did you see instead? Expect to see a full list of all installed packages.
comments:
@harrisonravazzolo the list of locations that osquery checks for Python packages is here: https://github.com/osquery/osquery/blob/master/osquery/tables/system/python_packages.cpp#L35 Do you know if the ones listed by `pip3` are installed in one of those locations?  You can ask it for the per-package install paths with `pip3 list -v`.

Are these packages installed only for your user (user-site packages)? (`pip3 list --user` to list only user-site packages, versus `pip3 list --local` to list only system-installed packages) Many tables in osquery are still unable to report information in a per-user context other than its own (osquery typically running as admin). From a short look at the source linked above I think maybe osquery won't list user-site packages.

Lastly, if you have Xcode and Homebrew installed, you might have more than one Python 3 and more than one pip3 on the PATH. Here's what I get on a macOS Sequoia system:

```shell
➜  ~ /usr/local/bin/pip3 list -v
Package   Version   Location                                Installer
--------- --------- --------------------------------------- ---------
certifi   2024.8.30 /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages brew
packaging 24.2      /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages brew
pip       24.2      /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages pip
wheel     0.44.0    /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages pip

➜  ~ /usr/bin/pip3 list -v
Package    Version Location                                                                                                                 Installer
---------- ------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------
altgraph   0.17.2  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
future     0.18.2  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
macholib   1.15.2  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
pip        21.2.4  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
setuptools 58.0.4  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
six        1.15.0  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
wheel      0.37.0  /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Library/Frameworks/Python3.framework/Versions/3.9/lib/python3.9/site-packages pip
```

But if running osquery, I actually see far _more_ packages than pip3 lists.

```
osquery> select COUNT(*) from python_packages;
+----------+
| COUNT(*) |
+----------+
| 43       |
+----------+
```

because it finds the Python installs at `/usr/local/lib/python3.9/`, `/usr/local/lib/python3.10/`, `/usr/local/lib/python3.11/`, `/usr/local/lib/python3.12/`, etc. But it does not list anything from the Xcode-managed Python.

@michael-myers - Interesting! When I run `pip3 list -v` from my test vm, almost of them are indeed installed for the user

`/Users/miso/Library/Python/3.9/lib/python/site-packages`

Ah, then that is probably it. It seems that a while back, someone added the ability to specify a custom directory for this table to search. I don't know if that is helpful here, e.g., `select * from python_packages where directory='/somedirectory/';`

@michael-myers thanks for the helpful analysis! @harrisonravazzolo it does seem like specifying the directory would be a workaround.

We should understand how your Python is installed and then consider updating the default paths that osquery checks.

I installed python via [pyenv](https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv). 
```
$ which python
/Users/ksykulev/.pyenv/shims/python
$ pip install numpy
Collecting numpy
  Using cached numpy-2.2.0-cp313-cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl.metadata (62 kB)
Using cached numpy-2.2.0-cp313-cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl (5.1 MB)
Installing collected packages: numpy
Successfully installed numpy-2.2.0
$ pip show numpy
....
Location: /Users/ksykulev/.pyenv/versions/3.13.1/lib/python3.13/site-packages
Requires: 
Required-by: pandas
```

I installed python via [python.org pkg](https://www.python.org/downloads/macos/).
```
$ which python3.13
/Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/bin/python3.13
$ pip3 install numpy
Collecting numpy
  Using cached numpy-2.2.0-cp313-cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl.metadata (62 kB)
Using cached numpy-2.2.0-cp313-cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl (5.1 MB)
Installing collected packages: numpy
Successfully installed numpy-2.2.0
$ pip3 show numpy
...
Location: /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.13/lib/python3.13/site-packages
Requires: 
Required-by: 
```

I installed python view [homebrew](https://brew.sh/)
```
$ which python3
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3
```
However, homebrew creates a virtual environment, so simply doing a pip install throws an error
```
$ pip3 install numpy
error: externally-managed-environment

× This environment is externally managed
╰─> To install Python packages system-wide, try brew install
    xyz, where xyz is the package you are trying to
    install.
    
    If you wish to install a Python library that isn't in Homebrew,
    use a virtual environment:
    
    python3 -m venv path/to/venv
    source path/to/venv/bin/activate
    python3 -m pip install xyz
    
    If you wish to install a Python application that isn't in Homebrew,
    it may be easiest to use 'pipx install xyz', which will manage a
    virtual environment for you. You can install pipx with
    
    brew install pipx
    
    You may restore the old behavior of pip by passing
    the '--break-system-packages' flag to pip, or by adding
    'break-system-packages = true' to your pip.conf file. The latter
    will permanently disable this error.
    
    If you disable this error, we STRONGLY recommend that you additionally
    pass the '--user' flag to pip, or set 'user = true' in your pip.conf
    file. Failure to do this can result in a broken Homebrew installation.
    
    Read more about this behavior here: <https://peps.python.org/pep-0668/>

note: If you believe this is a mistake, please contact your Python installation or OS distribution provider. You can override this, at the risk of breaking your Python installation or OS, by passing --break-system-packages.
hint: See PEP 668 for the detailed specification.
```


You need to either specify `--break-system-packages` or in your `pip.conf` set `break-system-packages = true`. In this case I am able to replicate the location.
```
$ pip3 install --break-system-packages --user numpy
Collecting numpy
  Using cached numpy-2.2.0-cp313-cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl.metadata (62 kB)
Using cached numpy-2.2.0-cp313-cp313-macosx_14_0_arm64.whl (5.1 MB)
Installing collected packages: numpy
  WARNING: The scripts f2py and numpy-config are installed in '/Users/ksykulev/Library/Python/3.13/bin' which is not on PATH.
  Consider adding this directory to PATH or, if you prefer to suppress this warning, use --no-warn-script-location.
Successfully installed numpy-2.2.0
$ pip3 show numpy
...
Location: /Users/ksykulev/Library/Python/3.13/lib/python/site-packages
Requires: 
Required-by: 
```


I was curious about the `--user` flag https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip_install/#cmdoption-user
If I use my homebrew installed python:
```
$ which python3
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3
$ python3
Python 3.13.1 (main, Dec  3 2024, 17:59:52) [Clang 16.0.0 (clang-1600.0.26.4)] on darwin
Type "help", "copyright", "credits" or "license" for more information.
>>> import site
>>> print(site.USER_BASE)
/Users/ksykulev/Library/Python/3.13
```
https://docs.python.org/3/library/site.html#site.USER_BASE

So this is what seemingly may cause the location of your packages to be in your user directory rather than typically `~/.local/`

Looks like that pyenv path wasn't covered either?

Maybe we need to add a couple of these user directory based paths?
The user's directory should come from a join to the users table like in the _extensions tables I think. If that join happens then the relevant subdirs would be searched.

review_comments: So are we running this for Windows too?

Does c++ do anything with allocating memory when you initialize a vector?
`std::vector<std::string> results;`

That's the only reason I kept it inside the `#ifdef WIN32`

But happy to move it out if you don't think it's a problem 👍
Fair, then maybe you can use`#elif`?
